tagline: Down in the bottoms where the Kaw meets the Missouri.
intro: It is a short city drive, and it starts low, in the West Bottoms where the Kansas River runs into the Missouri. Woodswether Road leads east toward downtown, and Berkley Parkway carries the route on to the Missouri riverfront.

The bottoms were a livestock and meatpacking district from 1871, with stockyards second only to Chicago's at their peak, and they were always prone to flood. The Great Flood of 1951 wrecked the yards for good. In the Second World War a plant at the mouth of the Kansas River built landing craft, one a day, and floated them more than 1,000 miles down the rivers to New Orleans. People called them Prairie Ships.

moments.title: Kaw Point
moments.text: Across the mouth of the Kansas River, Lewis and Clark camped three days in June 1804, mending pirogues and noting that the Missouri ran muddier than the Kaw.

moments.title: West Bottoms
moments.text: The brick buildings put up for stockyards, rail yards and factories now hold galleries, antique shops and haunted-house attractions.

moments.title: Berkley Riverfront Park
moments.text: On Berkley Parkway by the Missouri, the park takes the name of the mayor who championed cleaning up and redeveloping the old riverfront beside it.
